headline: Kyiv bridge hit during Merz visit; Yemen all-out push; VW picks Wayve over Nvidia.

stories.title: Russia hits Kyiv Northern Bridge as Merz meets Zelenskyy
facts: Material update to morning visit: Russia struck the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro during Merz’s surprise Kyiv trip — Klitschko cited road/hot-water disruption; second capital bridge hit this weekend.
Air-raid sirens and explosions marked the day; Merz and Zelenskyy met at the National Academy of Sciences (drone-hit Sep 28).
Merz (written statement): travelled because Ukraine needs support in the coming weeks; again: if Russia is not stopped, its war machine will turn on Europe.
Aid package still the morning frame: ~€1bn military (interceptor drones / long-range) + ~€350m energy repairs; Siemens Energy and Diehl Defence among accompanying execs.
stories.whyItMatters: The overnight story was the aid announcement; Sunday’s strike makes the security backdrop concrete while Merz is still in the capital.

image.alt: Russia hits Kyiv bridge as Germany’s Merz visits Ukraine’s capital

stories.title: Yemen’s government declares all-out war to retake Houthi territory
facts: President Rashad al-Alimi (televised, Sun): start of military operations to retake remaining republic territory and restore state authority nationwide.
Houthis (Yahya Saree): claimed ballistic + drone hits on Aramco in Riyadh and Khurais; Saudi yet to comment on Sunday’s claim (coalition earlier called Saturday’s Riyadh claim misleading).
AFP: Houthis cut a vital Taiz–Aden supply route, effectively encircling Taiz per Yemeni military sources.
Context: war reignited July; last month Houthis seized Red Sea coast / Bab al-Mandab leverage amid wider Iran–US conflict.
stories.whyItMatters: Morning covered the Aramco claim; evening adds an explicit government all-out campaign plus a Taiz logistics squeeze.

stories.title: Two tankers struck near Hormuz; Iran: strait stays shut until seven conditions
facts: UKMTO: crude tanker hit by unknown projectile ~4 nm east of Oman (Sat); another tanker struck Sun in the Strait of Hormuz with engine-room damage.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf (Nour News): Hormuz will not reopen until Iran’s seven Islamabad MoU conditions are met — halt to US “aggression,” end naval blockade/economic warfare, release of Iranian assets among them.
Brent closed Fri ~$102.25; WTI ~$91.11 after G7 stock release softened Thursday’s carrier-group spike.
stories.whyItMatters: Shipping hits keep energy risk live even when crude prints ease on strategic-release headlines.

stories.title: Ethiopian forces take Tigray capital Mekelle as TPLF withdraws
facts: TPLF (Sat night): “temporarily moved out of Mekelle” to operate elsewhere after federal army + allied fighters advanced.
Reuters/AFP: airport retaken earlier Sat; fighters entered city centre; humanitarian sources and a resident confirmed government control Sunday.
Fighting resumed Sep 23 after a seven-group alliance aimed at removing PM Abiy; 2022 peace deal had collapsed.
US State Dept urged Ethiopia and Eritrea to show restraint; Egypt’s el-Sisi (AU summit) stressed dialogue over confrontation.
stories.whyItMatters: Mekelle’s fall is the sharpest Tigray turn since the 2022 deal broke — with regional spillover risk already flagged by Washington and Cairo.

image.alt: Ethiopian government forces seize Tigray capital Mekelle as rebels withdraw

stories.title: VW picks London startup Wayve over Nvidia for autonomous driving
facts: SPIEGEL (insiders) + heise Sun: VW selected Wayve’s end-to-end AI driving stack after London city tests beat Nvidia and other bidders; final contract still unsigned (Audi procurement to negotiate).
Follows end of Cariad–Bosch Automated Driving Alliance; Level-2 system retained (e.g. ID.EVERY1); Wayve to supply AI software Cariad integrates into existing sensors/compute.
Wayve (~$2.8bn raised) also partners/investors with Mercedes, Nissan, Stellantis; Nvidia remains a Wayve investor and possible chip supplier.
stories.whyItMatters: Europe’s largest carmaker is choosing a UK foundation-model AD stack over a full Nvidia software pitch — a Cariad jobs/architecture story as much as a supplier swap.

stories.title: Reiche’s wind-lease cap draws bank and renewables fire
facts: EEG draft: 20-year Pachtdeckel at 3.5% of pre-ops gross annual yield (raised from 2.5% after consultation); EEG + Netzpaket targeted mid-October; Wirtschaftsausschuss hearing this week, key vote Oct 14.
18 banks (open letter): monitoring/penalty risk raises financing costs and undercuts intended savings; BEE and Waldeigentümer warn of fewer projects; di Fabio opinion calls cap unconstitutional.
BMWK still argues past high leases inflate EEG costs; VKU backs some cap but wants regional flexibility.
stories.whyItMatters: Separate from morning’s Rentenreform spat — this is Reiche’s cost-cut Energiewende package colliding with lenders and renewables lobbies before the mid-October vote.

facts.text: Trump names DNI Jay Clayton to lead a “Super Intelligence Force” (SIF) AI task force with FTC’s Ferguson, Pentagon CTO Emil Michael, OPM’s Kupor — 120-day assessment window.
ACI Europe / IATA / Amadeus / Sita / Idemia “Responsible Biometrics” coalition pushes Digital Omnibus rules for voluntary airport face ID; EDSA proportionality stance called too strict.
Photoshop beta Relight: reposition/soften/recolor light on finished photos; free low-res preview, 30 generative credits per final render (Fstoppers / Jesús Ramirez).
DGB, IG Metall, Verdi, Caritas, Diakonie, VdK urge halt to Pflegereform grade-tightening and other social cuts after Wednesday’s Kabinett draft.
